qt: to the Commission Daniel Buda (PPE) Subject:

Artificial intelligence and precision farming can reduce the use of inputs and improve the farm productivity and competitiveness. However, the Commission acknowledges that the uptake of digital technologies in the European agri-food sector remains slow and access to quality data is patchy. Initiatives such as the Common European Agricultural Data Space, agriculture of data and AI factories aim to speed up this transition. 1.

What total funding does the Commission plan to mobilise between 2028 and 2034 for the uptake of AI, precision farming and digital technologies by farms, and what portion of this funding will be directly accessible to small and medium-sized farms?
What measurable targets and timeline does the Commission have for the number or share of EU farms that should be using AI solutions and precision farming by 2030 or 2034?

When will the Common European Agricultural Data Space become fully operational and how will the Commission ensure that farmers remain in control of the data generated by their holdings and benefit economically from its use?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (27.11.2026) Building on the current period and synergies offered within the next Multiannual Financial Framework, farmers’ uptake of digital and artificial intelligence (AI) tools will be supported in the 2028-2034 period mainly under the National and Regional Partnership Plans (NRPP), in particular via the Common Agricultural Policy. Member States may design, according to their needs, investments, agri-environment and climate actions, innovation, advisory and skills measures to support digital uptake, including targeted support for small and mediumsized farms. Additional support can be mobilised via the proposed Horizon Europe and European Competitiveness Fund to support sectoral AI and digital deployment. In 2028-2034, farm digitalisation is a dedicated intervention field in the Annex I of the proposed Performance Regulation1, allowing systematic monitoring of expenditure and measures while the related output and result indicators will capture the effects of the support. These indicators, together with the broader 2030 Digital Decade targets, provide the basis for assessing progress. No EU‑wide target has been set for digitalisation in agriculture, but Member States may set their own milestones and targets within the NRPP for 2034. The Commission closely monitors the implementation of the Common European Agricultural Data Space (CEADS) to be finalised in March 2028. CEADS will facilitate trusted data sharing while protecting farmers’ rights, supporting control of their data and reducing dependence on technology providers. By enabling data sharing for precision farming, supplychain optimisation and digital services, it can create opportunities for lower production costs, improved productivity and new revenue streams.
1 Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council, establishing a budget expenditure
tracking and performance framework and other horizontal rules for the Union programmes and activities, COM(2025) 545 final.
